reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the November 2 close, data fresh: SPX 7,541.40 is 3.86% below its 120-day high, 1.99% below its 50-day but still 3.13% above its 200-day; SMH at $508.31 sits between zones after a 24.34% drawdown and 2.26% below its 200-day, NVDA at $202.06 occupies Zone 1, VIX is 21.15 at its 5-day high, HY OAS is 3.43% and calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4 with no volume climax and no VIX rollover. The midday tape bounces (QQQ +0.76% intraday, VIX 20.36) but the settled episode is unchanged.
reaction.invalidation: A close above SPX 7,820 with SMH reclaiming its 50-day average ($571.57) and VIX rolling over would prove the correction over and void the Watch stance; conversely HY OAS above 4% would prove it was never just a correction. Either print voids this ladder.

ladder.response: Arm Tranche A prep: 25% deployment only if the capitulation tally reaches 3 of 4 (volume climax or VIX rollover joining zone occupancy and credit calm); otherwise hold bills and wait for the tally.

ladder.response: Treat as the trap case: no chasing, no new entries; hold cash and wait for the retest verdict — the midday bounce is the first attempt and is expected to fail, not a buying opportunity.

ladder.response: Stand down: the correction becomes a crack or a trend break, the ladder below is void, and the thesis is reassessed from scratch before any deployment.

ladder.response: Probe tier-A conviction names (AVGO, DDOG) at no more than 20% of intended weight; add only on confirmation, never on the first bounce.
ladder.trigger: Second low holds above the first low with VIX rolling over from 21.15 and an SMH volume climax reversal

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the live risk today: the midday bounce (QQQ +0.76%, NVDA +3.1%, CONL +16.5% intraday) has no volume climax and no VIX rollover behind it, and NVDA sitting in Zone 1 alone is not a buy signal. Entries wait for the second low to hold plus a VIX rollover; chasing the first bounce converts a Watch stance into a trapped long.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is real but unconfirmed as a bottom: the midday tape bounces (QQQ +0.76% intraday, NVDA +3.1%) yet the settled tally is 2 of 4 with no volume climax or VIX rollover, and NVDA sits in Zone 1 while SMH sits below its 200-day. New money stays in bills until Zone 2 prints or a confirmed second low.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the base case only while credit stays calm. The divergence itself is real and worth tracking: if lending standards or HY OAS flip, the same price action re-reads as a rollover. Do not buy the dip on index calm alone — the leadership that drove the index is the part that is breaking.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 16.07% below their 52-week highs versus SPX 3.3% below its high — a 12.77-point divergence gap, with GOOGL the weakest at -31.8% and AAPL the strongest at -6%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is 3.43% with credit marked calm, not cracking. Today's breadth supports the rotation read: IWM is +0.82% and QQQ +0.76% intraday while the Mag7 laggards stay deep in the red.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — Mag7 unwinds while the index holds
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market break: QQQ is down 9.25% in a month and the AI complex is deep in the red, which the news frames as a rollover. The index disagrees — SPX is only 3.86% off its 120-day high at 7,541.40.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4% or SLOOS tightening toward stress levels would void the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Cheap on growth is not a floor. RSI readings in the 30s and low 40s across the chain (NVDA 41.1, AVGO 45.2, LRCX 33.2, AMAT 35.9) say oversold, not bottomed — no volume climax reversal has printed and VIX is still at its 5-day high on a settled basis. The setup is real, but the entry trigger has not fired; buying the first bounce is the trap case.

themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market is pricing AI infrastructure as a busted trade: SMH is down 24.34% from its high and 19.81% in 20 days, NVDA is down 12.8% in a month, and the whole semiconductor chain sits 25-50% below 52-week highs.
themes.watchFor: SMH volume climax with intraday reversal plus VIX rolling over from 21.15 would confirm a tradeable low in the complex.

themes.counterRead: A bounce is not a bottom. The settled tape says the opposite of confirmation: SMH volume was 0.92x its 20-day average on November 2 with the close in the bottom 7% of the day's range, VIX closed at its 5-day high of 21.15 with no rollover, and SMH sits 2.26% below its 200-day. The bounce has to survive the close and then the failure-zone retest before it means anything.
themes.dataAnchor: The intraday tape is green across the beaten-down complex: SPY +0.44%, QQQ +0.76%, NVDA +3.1% (live $208.44 vs settled $202.06), COIN +8.36%, BMNR +5.04%, TQQQ +2.15%, CONL +16.5%. VIX is 20.36 intraday, down 3.74% from the settled 21.15. But every one of those moves is unconfirmed — the mechanical tally is still 2 of 4, and the episode block is settled November 2 closes, not today's intraday prints.
themes.label: Midday bounce: a trap test, not a bottom
themes.narrative: The market opened higher and the worst-hit names are ripping intraday, which reads as the bottom being in. The settled data says the bounce is the first attempt, and first attempts in a correction usually fail at the failure zone.
themes.watchFor: Whether today's close holds the bounce — a fade back to red by the close, or a bounce into SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH $580-600 that rejects, confirms the trap case.

themes.counterRead: Bonds are not rescuing equities here: the 10-year at 4.94% with a Fed signaling higher rates means the correction has no rate-cut put. The guardrail is credit, not rates — if HY OAS breaks 4%, the episode stops being a correction and becomes a crack, and the whole ladder below is void.
themes.dataAnchor: Money is tight but credit is not cracking: DFF 3.88%, DGS2 4.56%, DGS10 4.94%, DGS30 5.31%, real 10-year 2.65%, 2s10s curve +0.38, HY OAS 3.43% and explicitly marked calm. VIX is 21.15 settled, up 36.28% in 20 days and at its 5-day high, but that is a fear print without a credit event behind it — the mechanical tally confirms credit-calm as one of its two confirmed signals.
themes.label: Rates and credit: tight money, calm credit — the correction's guardrail
themes.narrative: The Fed is signaling higher rates — the October 27-28 FOMC is still the active high-signal event and the December 8-9 meeting is already anticipated — and the 10-year sits at 4.94% with the 2s10s curve at +0.38.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or a December FOMC surprise would break the calm-credit guardrail.

themes.counterRead: Event-week volatility cuts both ways: a clean AMD print tonight or a midterm result the market reads as gridlock could fuel the bounce into the failure zone — the trap case. Do not let one good print reclassify a correction that has not confirmed a low. And the Labs line is already lost: QQQ closed Monday at $681.09, below the $684.40 trigger, so the Labs host sells at today's open under their rule (not Jun's); today's intraday $686.23 does not un-trigger a close-based rule.

themes.narrative: The week is stacked with binary events — US midterm elections today, AMD earnings after the close tonight, and the October jobs report Friday November 6 — and the market is pricing that uncertainty with VIX up 31.19% in a month.
themes.watchFor: AMD's print tonight and the October jobs report Friday November 6; either can set the week's direction, neither confirms a bottom on its own.
